text: The map sends m⊗c to Σ(m⊗c₁)⊗c₂ by applying the supplied coproduct and reassociating. CoalgebraStruct supplies maps without imposing their laws, so this is only a candidate coaction at this generality. With the coalgebra laws, it becomes the cofree construction of [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); no coaction on M is required. Checks pass: [cofreeCoact_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L87), [cofree_coact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L157).
The map is exactly id⊗Δ followed by inverse reassociation.
The selected cofree structure evaluates by the stated coproduct formula.

On m⊗c the candidate map is the inverse associator applied to m⊗Δ(c), yielding Σ(m⊗c₁)⊗c₂. The formula uses only CoalgebraStruct, which supplies linear coproduct and counit data without their laws. It gives the underlying tensor formula for [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); it does not alone certify a comodule structure. Checks pass: [cofreeCoact_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L87), [cofree_coact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L157).
The map is the specified coproduct composite.
Under actual coalgebra laws the selected cofree structure has this same formula.

The coproduct equips M⊗C with its cofree right C-comodule structure. Coassociativity and the counit law come directly from those of C, implementing [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The construction explicitly selects this coaction because a tensor module may carry others; neither multiplication on C nor a coaction on M is required. Checks pass: [cofree_coact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L157), [rTensor_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L164).
The packaged coaction has the expected value on elementary tensors.
The middle-factor counit gives the retraction used by the universal property.

The coaction of the selected cofree structure is id_M⊗Δ_C followed by reassociation into (M⊗C)⊗C. This identifies the actual structure implementing [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The equation concerns that particular coaction on M⊗C, rather than every possible comodule structure on the same carrier; tensor associativity changes parentheses, not factor order. Checks pass: [cofreeCoact_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L87), [cofree_coact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L157).
The implementation unfolds to precisely the same linear composite.
The identified composite gives the coproduct formula on pure tensors.

On an elementary tensor m⊗c, the cofree coaction is Σ(m⊗c₁)⊗c₂, with Δ(c)=Σc₁⊗c₂. This is the tensor-comonad instance of [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The displayed inverse associator accounts for parentheses; the formula does not select a basis or require any particular presentation of the coproduct as a sum. Checks pass: [cofreeCoact_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L87), [rTensor_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L164).
The underlying map applies the coproduct to the right factor.
Applying the counit to c₁ recovers the original tensor.

After coacting on m⊗c, this composite applies ε to the middle coefficient c₁, giving Σm⊗ε(c₁)c₂=m⊗c. The tensor-unit map absorbs the scalar into M. This is the counit retraction used in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); specifying the actual factor avoids ambiguity about the names of the left and right counit laws. Checks pass: [cofree_coact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L157), [cofreeLift_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L314).
The coaction exposes the two coefficient factors in their actual order.
The retraction recovers a comodule morphism from its counit component.

A linear map f:M→N induces f⊗id_C between the cofree comodules, leaving the coalgebra coefficient unchanged. Naturality of the coproduct proves compatibility with their coactions. This is the morphism operation of the cofree functor in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); neither M nor N needs a prior comodule structure. Checks pass: [cofreeMap_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L196), [cofreeMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L215).
The underlying map is exactly f⊗id_C.
The construction preserves composition of linear maps.

The coaction ρ_P itself is a comodule morphism P→P⊗C when the target carries the cofree coaction. Its compatibility is precisely coassociativity of ρ_P. This gives the unit of the forgetful–cofree adjunction in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); the word unit refers to that adjunction, not to a multiplicative identity in C. Checks pass: [cofreeUnit_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L236), [cofreeUnit_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L242).
The underlying linear map is the original coaction.
Evaluation retains the actual value ρ_P(p).

An ordinary linear map g:P→M from a C-comodule lifts to (g⊗id_C)ρ_P:P→M⊗C. Coassociativity makes this a comodule morphism into the cofree target, realizing the inverse correspondence in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The map g need not preserve any coaction on M, because no such coaction is assumed. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L254), [rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeLift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L308).
The lift has exactly the stated underlying composite.
Taking its counit component recovers the original map g.

The lifted comodule morphism has underlying linear map (g⊗id_C)ρ_P. Thus the construction adds a compatibility proof without changing that composite, as required by the cofree correspondence of [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The notation rTensor places g on the left carrier factor and leaves the right coalgebra coefficient unchanged. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L260), [rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeLift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L308).
Evaluation agrees with applying g to the carrier factor of the coaction.
The counit projection returns g.

The cofree lift sends p to (g⊗id_C)(ρ_P(p)), or Σg(p₀)⊗p₁ in Sweedler notation. This concretely evaluates the inverse correspondence in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The coaction value can be any tensor, including a sum of elementary tensors; neither a basis nor a finite-dimensionality assumption is needed. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L254), [cofreeEquiv_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L302).
The full linear map is the same composite.
The inverse of the universal correspondence is precisely this lift.

The cofree correspondence is an R-linear equivalence: φ maps to its counit component, and g maps back to (g⊗id_C)ρ. Both inverse identities follow from coaction compatibility and counitality, as in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). Linearity additionally preserves addition and scalar multiplication on morphisms; no flatness or finite-dimensionality is required. Checks pass: [rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeLift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L308), [cofreeLift_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L314), [add_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L70), [smul_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L75).
Counit projection after lifting returns the linear map.
Lifting the counit component returns the comodule morphism.
The domain addition is the ordinary pointwise addition used by the linearity field.
The domain scalar operation is ordinary pointwise scalar multiplication.

The forward universal correspondence sends φ:P→M⊗C to its counit component πφ, where π(m⊗c)=ε(c)m. The right tensor-unit identification absorbs the scalar into M. This is the explicit forward map in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); φ is a comodule morphism, and the result is an ordinary linear map. Checks pass: [rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeLift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L308), [cofreeLift_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L314).
This forward map undoes the cofree lift.
The same counit component determines φ uniquely.

The inverse universal correspondence sends an ordinary linear map g:P→M to the cofree lift (g⊗id_C)ρ_P. This is the inverse of the counit-component map in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The inverse acts between spaces of morphisms; it does not assert that g, the coaction, or the counit projection is invertible. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L260), [rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeLift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L308).
The inverse has the concrete value (g⊗id_C)(ρ_P(p)).
Taking the counit component recovers g.

Applying π(m⊗c)=ε(c)m after the cofree lift of g returns g. Indeed, the counit law for P reduces Σg(p₀)ε(p₁) to g(p). This is one inverse identity of [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The tensor-unit map performs scalar multiplication in M, rather than discarding the scalar coefficient. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L254), [cofreeEquiv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L293).
The lift is the carrier-map tensor identity composed with the coaction.
The forward correspondence is exactly this counit projection.

A comodule morphism φ:P→M⊗C is recovered by lifting its counit component πφ. Colinearity of φ and the coalgebra counit law give this inverse identity of [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The comodule-morphism hypothesis is essential: the statement does not claim that an arbitrary linear map into M⊗C is determined by its counit component. Checks pass: [cofreeEquiv_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L302), [rTensor_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L164).
The inverse correspondence is the specified lift.
The middle-factor counit retraction supplies the recovery identity.

A comodule morphism into M⊗C is zero exactly when its counit component is zero. The R-linear cofree equivalence realizes [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), so injectivity and preservation of zero give this equivalence. It detects zero among compatible morphisms into the cofree target; the counit projection M⊗C→M itself need not be injective. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L314), [cofreeEquiv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L293).
Every such morphism is reconstructed from its counit component.
The bijection uses exactly the stated counit projection.

The zero linear map is a comodule morphism because both sides of its intertwining equation vanish. This supplies zero in the morphism space of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), specialized to tensor coactions. No zero object or trivial coaction is being assigned to either carrier; their given comodule structures are retained. Checks pass: [zero_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L65), [zero_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L186).
The constructed morphism has underlying zero map.
Its composite on the left is again zero.

Adding two comodule morphisms pointwise gives another: linearity of the coactions and tensor map lets their intertwining equations add. This makes the compatibility diagram in [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6) closed under addition for these comodules. The sum is addition of maps, not composition, and requires no multiplication on the coefficient coalgebra. Checks pass: [add_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L86), [comp_add](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L163).
The sum evaluates pointwise.
Composition distributes over this addition in its right argument.

Multiplying a comodule morphism by r∈R pointwise preserves its intertwining equation, since both coactions are R-linear. This supplies scalar multiplication on the morphism space described by [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The base semiring is commutative, making scalar multiples of linear maps linear; this is not an action by arbitrary coalgebra elements. Checks pass: [smul_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L97), [comp_smul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L178).
The scalar multiple evaluates to r times the original value.
Composition respects this scalar multiplication.

Forgetting coaction compatibility from f+g gives the sum of their underlying linear maps. Thus the addition used in the linear cofree correspondence is exactly ordinary pointwise addition. Its compatibility follows by adding the intertwining equations of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); the theorem does not identify addition of maps with their composition. Checks pass: [add_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L86), [add_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L156).
Evaluation confirms the pointwise sum.
Composition is additive in its left argument.

Forgetting compatibility from r•f returns r times the underlying linear map. This identifies the scalar operation used in the R-linear cofree correspondence and follows directly from its construction. The intertwining equation of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6) is preserved by R-linearity; the scalar comes from the commutative base, not from the coefficient coalgebra. Checks pass: [smul_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L97), [smul_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L170).
The underlying scalar operation evaluates pointwise.
Composition is compatible with scalar multiplication in the left argument.

Comodule morphisms form a commutative additive monoid under pointwise zero and addition, with all laws inherited from the target module. This equips the morphisms of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6) with their expected additive structure. Natural-number multiplication means repeated addition, including zero repetitions; additive inverses are not assumed over a general semiring. Checks pass: [nsmul_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L141), [sum_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L146).
Repeated addition agrees with pointwise natural-number multiplication.
Finite sums become ordinary sums of underlying linear maps.

The map forgetting coaction compatibility preserves zero and sums, so it is an additive homomorphism from comodule morphisms to ordinary linear maps. It records the additive structure on the compatible maps of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The underlying function is simply f↦f; this forgetful map is not asserted to reach every linear map. Checks pass: [zero_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L65), [add_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L70).
The forgetful map preserves zero.
It preserves the chosen addition.

The compatible linear maps form an R-module with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication. The intertwining equation of [Wisbauer §1.13](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6) is linear in the morphism, and the source transfers the module laws through the injective forgetful map. Over a semiring, Module means a semimodule: additive inverses need not exist. Checks pass: [smul_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L75), [add_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Hom.lean#L70).
The transferred scalar operation is pointwise scalar multiplication.
The transferred addition is pointwise addition.

A nonnegative real is constructed from a real value x together with evidence that x≥0. The resulting value is exactly x; nothing is rounded, clipped or replaced by an absolute value. Unlike the total conversion from arbitrary reals, this constructor requires nonnegativity before it can be used. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L75).

Zero is the ordinary real zero equipped with its nonnegativity evidence. It is the least nonnegative real and, under the surrounding arithmetic structures, the additive identity and an absorbing multiplier. This type contains only finite values, so its zero is distinct from any extended-real infinity convention. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L77).

One is the ordinary real one, regarded as a nonnegative real. The surrounding multiplication has this value as its identity, and it differs from zero. No rounding, reduction modulo a characteristic, or rescaling is involved: converting this value back to a real gives exactly one. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L78).

Nonnegative reals inherit the ordinary real comparison, with reflexivity, transitivity and antisymmetry. Equality is equality of the underlying real values, regardless of the nonnegativity evidence used to construct them. This declaration supplies the partial-order laws; total comparability is provided separately by the linear-order structure. Compared with [Faris §5.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

Any two nonnegative reals are comparable in the usual real order, and strict comparison has its ordinary meaning. The structure inherits these relations from real numbers. Lean marks the construction noncomputable; the availability of logical comparisons does not supply an algorithm for deciding inequalities between arbitrary described real numbers. Compared with [Faris §5.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L91).

Zero is the least nonnegative real: every value is at least zero by its definition. This gives a bottom element, not a greatest element. Nonnegative reals are unbounded above, so the order structure does not introduce an infinity value or turn arbitrary unbounded sets into sets with finite suprema. Compared with [Faris §§5.1, 5.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

Nonnegative reals are closed under ordinary addition and multiplication, with zero and one. These operations satisfy the semiring laws: associative multiplication, commutative addition, distributivity and zero absorption. Additive inverses are not required, so the absence of negative numbers is compatible with this structure; multiplication’s commutativity is packaged separately. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

Nonnegative reals form a commutative semiring with their usual addition and multiplication. Multiplication commutes, distributes over addition, and has identity one; zero absorbs multiplication. This remains a semiring rather than a ring because positive values have no additive inverses within the nonnegative domain. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

Addition of nonnegative reals is associative and commutative, has identity zero, and permits cancellation: a+c=b+c implies a=b. Cancellation follows from ordinary real addition and does not require additive inverses to belong to this domain. In particular, it does not make subtraction an unrestricted inverse operation. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

The usual order on nonnegative reals agrees with adding a nonnegative difference: a≤b exactly when b=a+c for some nonnegative c. When a≤b, the ordinary difference b−a supplies that witness. This explains the canonical additive order without asserting that negative differences belong to the type. Compared with [Faris §§2.5, 5.2](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

A product of two nonnegative reals is zero only if at least one factor is zero. The converse also holds by zero absorption. This is the inherited real-number property, and it permits cancellation of nonzero factors; multiplication by zero still loses all information and cannot be cancelled. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

For every nonnegative x and every strictly positive y, some natural-number multiple of y is at least x. Thus even an arbitrarily small positive step can eventually reach any prescribed finite value. The requirement y>0 matters: repeated addition of zero cannot reach a positive target. Compared with [Kiming Theorem 3(1)](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

Every nonempty bounded-above set of nonnegative reals has a supremum, and every nonempty set has an infimum since zero is a lower bound. Lean also defines exceptional cases: an unbounded set’s supremum is zero, and both empty-set extrema are zero. These defaults do not assert that zero bounds an unbounded set. Compared with [Faris §§2.7, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L452).

The least upper bound of two nonnegative reals is their ordinary maximum. It remains nonnegative and is one of the two inputs because the order is linear. This binary supremum operation does not require a greatest element and does not itself assert existence of suprema for arbitrary sets. Compared with [Faris §5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

The greatest lower bound of two nonnegative reals is their ordinary minimum, which remains nonnegative. In particular, the minimum of zero and any value is zero. This binary infimum agrees with real order and is distinct from the separately defined infimum of an empty or arbitrary set. Compared with [Faris §5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L81).

Reciprocal of a positive nonnegative real is its ordinary real reciprocal. At zero, Lean defines the reciprocal as zero, keeping the operation within finite nonnegative reals. This differs from the extended nonnegative reals, whose reciprocal of zero is infinity; inverse-cancellation laws therefore require a nonzero input. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L99).

A nonnegative rational is represented as the same nonnegative real value. The rational number 5/2 therefore becomes 2.5, without rounding or natural-number division. The domain already excludes negative rationals, so this operation is an exact inclusion rather than the clipping used when converting arbitrary real numbers. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L97).

Integer powers of nonnegative reals use ordinary real powers: positive exponents are repeated multiplication and negative exponents use reciprocals. For a positive base, the usual rules apply. Lean’s total conventions give 0⁰=1 and zero raised to a negative integer equal to zero, rather than infinity or an undefined value. Compared with [Faris §2.5](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L108).

The inclusion of nonnegative reals into the real numbers preserves zero, one, addition and multiplication. It is injective, with range exactly [0,∞), so it is not onto all reals. Lean’s ring-homomorphism notation also covers semiring domains here; it does not assert that nonnegative reals have additive inverses. Compared with [Faris §§2.5, 6.2](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean#L247).

Floor and ceiling of a nonnegative real return natural numbers: the greatest natural number not exceeding it and the least natural number not less than it. They agree with ordinary integer floor and ceiling on this domain. For example, 2.5 gives floor 2 and ceiling 3; both send zero to zero. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Basic.lean#L39).

For |w|<1, this is the boundary H² vector with holomorphic disk function k_w(z)=1/(1−w̄z). H² uses circle measure of total mass one and identifies functions equal almost everywhere. Pairing ⟨k_w,x⟩ evaluates x’s holomorphic extension at w; the inner product is conjugate-linear first. The open-disk restriction makes the denominator nonzero. See [Neeb, Example4.5.6, p.82](https://www.math.fau.de/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/rep14.pdf). Native Checks pass: [Pairing with the actual kernel evaluates the holomorphic disk function](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Analysis/Fourier/Hardy/ReproducingKernel.lean#L63), [The actual kernel has disk function 1/(1−w̄z)](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Analysis/Fourier/Hardy/ReproducingKernel.lean#L86), [Its squared norm equals 1/(1−|w|²)](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Analysis/Fourier/Hardy/ReproducingKernel.lean#L98), [The positive real normalization has norm one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Analysis/Fourier/Hardy/ReproducingKernel.lean#L143).
Pairing with the actual kernel evaluates the holomorphic disk function.
The actual kernel has disk function 1/(1−w̄z).
Its squared norm equals 1/(1−|w|²).
The positive real normalization has norm one.

A triangulating homeomorphism must be Cⁿ on every closed simplex, with derivative injective along that simplex’s directions, including at its boundary. In barycentric coordinates these directions have coordinate sum zero. This matches the usual notion for n≥1. At n=0 the definition still demands an injective derivative, so it is stronger than a merely continuous triangulation. See [Milnor–Stasheff, §20, p.240](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/milnstas.pdf). Native Checks pass: [The standard interval triangulation satisfies the actual predicate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/SmoothTriangulation/Basic.lean#L293), [The smooth squared-interval homeomorphism fails the derivative condition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/SmoothTriangulation/Basic.lean#L362).
The standard interval triangulation satisfies the actual predicate.
The smooth squared-interval homeomorphism fails the derivative condition.

Over any real closed ordered field, prescribing signs of p and every formal derivative gives an empty set, a singleton, or an open interval, possibly unbounded. “Subsingleton” includes emptiness; the added endpoints denote −∞ and +∞. Derivatives beyond the degree vanish, and the zero polynomial realizes exactly the all-zero prescription on the whole field. See [Basu–Pollack–Roy, Proposition2.27, p.42](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~gasarch/COURSES/752/S26/slides/AlgorithmsInRealAlgGeom.pdf). Native Checks pass: [The zero polynomial has zero sign at every derivative order and every point](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Polynomial/Thom/Basic.lean#L81), [Every derivative sign beyond the polynomial degree is zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Polynomial/Thom/Basic.lean#L90).
The zero polynomial has zero sign at every derivative order and every point.
Every derivative sign beyond the polynomial degree is zero.
